title: Problems in the Church are not new.
paragraphs: Problems in the Church are not new.
Read that again.

The corruption.
The compromise.
The hypocrisy.
The silence.
None of it surprised God then, and none of it surprises Him now.

From the wilderness complaints of Israel, to the rebellion of Korah, to the idolatry of kings, to the pride of religious leaders, Scripture never hides the ugliness of what happens when people who claim God’s name resist God’s voice. But here’s what most people don’t realize…

The real danger is not just that problems exist.
The real danger is when God’s people pretend they do not.

That is how small cracks become collapsed walls.
That is how tolerated sin becomes protected culture.
That is how wolves find open doors.
That is how wounded sheep bleed in silence while leaders polish appearances.
And the Church cannot heal what it refuses to confront.
This is why sound teaching matters. This is why discernment matters. This is why truth spoken in love matters.
Because the issue is never merely “church drama.”
It is sin.

It is pride that does not want exposure.
It is fear that does not want confrontation.
It is flesh that wants comfort more than holiness.
It is leadership without repentance.
It is membership without discernment.
It is religion without the fear of God.
And once sin is normalized in the house of God, many suffer under what few are willing to name.
But do not miss this.

Jesus did not die so His Church could become a museum for hidden corruption.
He died to sanctify her.
To cleanse her.
To purify for Himself a people marked by truth, repentance, and grace.

That means biblical correction is not hatred.
Exposure is not always attack.
Warning is not always rebellion.
And repentance is not weakness.
Sometimes the most loving thing you can do is stop protecting what God is trying to expose.

Originally written by Gospel Warrior, this is your reminder that silence can look spiritual while feeding destruction underneath. And if this found you, it’s not by accident. Follow the source, not the noise.

Still, correction without the Gospel becomes cruelty.
And truth without Jesus becomes a weapon in the hands of proud people.
So let us be clear.

The answer to problems in the Church is not cynicism.
It is not gossip.
It is not self-righteous outrage.
It is not abandoning Christ because people failed Him.
The answer is repentance.

Not theirs only.
Ours too.
Because judgment begins in the house of God, and revival begins when the people of God stop defending what Jesus died to destroy.

Sin must be named.
Pride must be broken.
Hidden things must come into the light.
And then comes the mercy.

Because the Gospel does not end with exposure.
It leads to redemption.

Jesus Christ stepped into the scandal of human sin, carried the full weight of our rebellion on the cross, shed His blood for the guilty, and rose again in power so that corrupt hearts could be made new. Salvation is not earned by cleaner behavior or stronger church culture. It is by grace through faith in Christ alone.

That means the liar can repent.
The compromised leader can repent.
The bitter member can repent.
The wounded believer can be restored.
The drifting church can return.

There is grace, but not grace that excuses sin.
Grace that saves.
Grace that transforms.
Grace that brings dead things back to life.
So no, problems in the Church are not new.

But ignoring them allows them to grow.
Confronting them biblically allows healing to begin.
And bringing them to Jesus is the only way anything truly changes.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…

God is still purifying His Church.
He is still calling people out of performance and into holiness.
He is still exposing darkness to reveal His light.
He is still saving sinners, restoring the broken, and building a Bride that belongs to Christ alone.

So do not just shake your head at the condition of the Church.
Fall on your knees.

Pray.
Repent.
Stand on Scripture.
Test every spirit.
Reject compromise.
Love the truth.
Point people to Jesus.
